statement:
Build a calculator as a single static HTML file named `index.html` in the repo root.

Requirements:
- A display, and a keypad of buttons: digits 0-9, a decimal point, the four operators
  (add, subtract, multiply, divide), equals, and clear.
- Pressing digits builds the current entry and shows it in the display. Pressing 1 then 2
  then 3 shows `123`. The decimal point adds a decimal point to the entry; an entry can
  contain at most one.
- A number, an operator, a second number, then equals shows the result. `7 + 8 =` shows `15`.
- Clear (AC) resets everything. The display shows `0`.
- The di...

title: Build a single-file calculator
statement: Build a calculator as a single static HTML file named `index.html` in the repo root with display, keypad, and specified interactions.
acceptance: index.html created in repo root with inline CSS and JS
Display element shows entry as typed, with data-value holding String(Number(entry))
Digits 0-9 build current entry; pressing 1, 2, 3 shows 123
Decimal point adds to entry; at most one per entry
Operators chain left to right: 7 + 8 + shows 15
Equals shows result rounded to 15 significant digits (e.g., 0.1 + 0.2 shows 0.3)
Clear (AC) resets to display 0
Display starts at 0
All required data-testid attributes present and correct
No frameworks, no build step, no CDN links, no network requests
sub_requirements: Display and keypad with correct buttons and attributes
Digit and decimal input builds entry
Operator chaining and equals computation
Clear resets state

title: Add chained calculations.
statement:
Add chained calculations.

- Pressing an operator while an operation is already waiting applies that waiting operation
  first and shows the running result. After `2 + 3`, pressing the multiply key shows `5`.
- Any number of operations can be chained before equals. `1 + 2 + 3 + 4 =` shows `10`.

Decision — how expressions are evaluated. This holds for the rest of the project:
- The calculator uses immediate execution. Each operator key finishes the operation already
  waiting, strictly left to right. There is no operator precedence.
  `2 + 3 × 4 =` is `20`, not `14`.
- Reason: this is how a po...

title: Chained calculations
statement: The calculator applies waiting operations when a new operator is pressed, and supports any number of chained operations evaluated left to right with no precedence.
acceptance: Pressing an operator while an operation is pending applies that operation first and displays the result
Multiple chained operations evaluate strictly left to right without operator precedence
2 + 3 × 4 = evaluates to 20, not 14
sub_requirements: Apply waiting operation when new operator is pressed
Support multiple chained operations before equals
Establish immediate execution (left-to-right, no precedence) as project rule

title: Two things: how numbers are shown, and division by zero.
statement:
Two things: how numbers are shown, and division by zero.

Decision — number presentation. This holds for the rest of the project:
- Round the displayed number to at most 10 significant digits.
- Drop trailing zeros after the decimal point, and drop a trailing decimal point.
  `1 ÷ 8 =` shows `0.125`. `4 ÷ 2 =` shows `2`. `2 ÷ 3 =` shows `0.6666666667`.
- No thousands separators. Use exponential notation only when the magnitude is 1e10 or
  larger, or smaller than 1e-9.
- The rounding happens only when the number is rendered. The value the calculator stores and
  computes with is never rounded,...

title: Number presentation and division by zero
statement: The calculator must present numbers with specific formatting rules and handle division by zero with an error state.
acceptance: Numbers displayed with at most 10 significant digits
Trailing zeros and decimal points removed from display
Exponential notation used only for magnitude ≥1e10 or <1e-9
Stored value and data-value attribute always hold exact unrounded value
Typed entry shown exactly as typed during user input
Division by zero shows 'Error' and sets data-error='true'
Error state ignores all keys except clear
Clear exits error state and resets display to 0
data-error attribute always present with 'true' or 'false'
sub_requirements: Number presentation: 10 significant digits, no trailing zeros, exponential notation threshold
Rounding only at render time, never in stored values
Division by zero error handling and state management

title: Add two single-key operations. Each acts on the current entry immediately.
statement:
Add two single-key operations. Each acts on the current entry immediately.

- `data-testid="key-sign"` — a `±` key that flips the sign of the current entry.
  `5 ±` shows `-5`, and pressing it again shows `5`.
- `data-testid="key-percent"` — a `%` key that divides the current entry by 100.
  `50 %` shows `0.5`.

title: Add two single-key operations
statement: Add ± and % keys that act on the current entry immediately.
acceptance: data-testid="key-sign" button displays ± and flips sign of current entry
5 ± shows -5, pressing again shows 5
Typed entries preserve text format when sign is flipped (1.50 becomes -1.50)
Results become their negative when sign is flipped
data-testid="key-percent" button displays % and divides current entry by 100
50 % shows 0.5
After % operation, typing a digit starts a new number (same behavior as after =)
% result is shown formatted
sub_requirements: ± key flips sign of current entry; preserves typed text format
% key divides current entry by 100 and shows formatted result

title: Add parentheses, so a user can group part of a calculation.
statement:
Add parentheses, so a user can group part of a calculation.

- `data-testid="key-lparen"` — the `(` key
- `data-testid="key-rparen"` — the `)` key
- `2 + ( 3 × 4 ) =` is `14`.
- `( 2 + 3 ) × 4 =` is `20`.
- Groups can be nested.

title: Add parentheses for grouping calculations
statement: Users can group part of a calculation using parentheses to override left-to-right evaluation.
acceptance: ( and ) keys present with data-testid="key-lparen" and data-testid="key-rparen"
2 + ( 3 × 4 ) = evaluates to 14
( 2 + 3 ) × 4 = evaluates to 20
Nested groups work
Pressing = closes any open groups
Unmatched ) does nothing

title: The `%` key is generating support tickets. People expect it to mean "percent of ...
statement:
The `%` key is generating support tickets. People expect it to mean "percent of the other
number" and it does not. Take the `%` key off the keypad.

Keep `±`. That one is fine and we still need it.

title: Remove % key from keypad
statement: Remove the % key from the calculator keypad and its associated code.
acceptance: % key removed from HTML keypad
inputPercent() function removed from JavaScript
Event handler for key-percent removed from dispatch logic
AC button widened to fill the gap left by % key
± key remains functional and unchanged
sub_requirements: Remove % key button from HTML
Remove inputPercent() function implementation
Remove event handler binding for % key
Maintain row alignment with AC button width adjustment
Keep ± key operational

title: Add a running tape of past calculations.
statement:
Add a running tape of past calculations.

- `data-testid="calc-tape"` — the tape container
- `data-testid="tape-row"` — one past calculation
- `data-testid="tape-expr"` — the expression, inside the row
- `data-testid="tape-result"` — its result, inside the row. Like `calc-display`, it also
  carries `data-value`, holding the exact result value as a plain number string, as
  produced by `String(value)`.
- `data-testid="tape-clear"` — a button that empties the tape

- A row is added each time equals completes a calculation. Newest row first.
- A row shows the expression and its result. Nothing e...

title: Running tape of past calculations
statement: The calculator must maintain a visible tape showing past calculations, with newest entries first, and provide a button to clear the tape.
acceptance: Tape container with data-testid='calc-tape' displays past calculations
Each tape row has data-testid='tape-row' containing expression (data-testid='tape-expr') and result (data-testid='tape-result')
Result element carries data-value attribute with String(value) of exact result
New row added to top of tape when equals (=) completes a calculation
Rows appear newest first
Expression shows how result was calculated with closed groups as single pieces (e.g., '−( 2 + 3 )')
Row added only when = has something to calculate; division by zero and standalone = add nothing
AC does not empty the tape
Clear button (data-testid='tape-clear') empties the tape without changing display
Tape shows expression and result only; no timestamps
sub_requirements: HTML structure: tape container, tape rows, expression and result elements
Tape row insertion: newest first
Expression building: with closed group handling
Clear button functionality: empties tape, leaves display unchanged

title: Bug report from a user:
statement:
Bug report from a user:

"The tape prints ugly numbers. I did 0.1 + 0.2 — the display showed 0.3, which is right, but
the line it wrote on the tape says 0.30000000000000004. Same thing with 1 ÷ 3: the display
looks fine and the tape is a mess. It's the same calculation. It should read the same in
both places."

Reproduce it and fix it.

title: Add memory keys.
statement:
Add memory keys.

- `data-testid="key-mplus"` — M+, adds the value currently displayed to memory.
- `data-testid="key-mr"` — MR, recalls the memory value into the display.
- `data-testid="key-mc"` — MC, clears memory back to zero.
- `data-testid="mem-indicator"` — shows whether memory is holding anything. It carries
  `data-active="true"` when memory is non-zero and `data-active="false"` when it is zero.

Memory starts at zero. Make sure memory respects the number behaviour we agreed on.

title: Add memory keys
statement: Calculator must support M+, MR, and MC memory keys, plus a memory indicator showing non-zero state.
acceptance: M+ key (data-testid="key-mplus") adds the exact displayed value to memory and finishes entry
MR key (data-testid="key-mr") recalls exact memory value into display as a result
MC key (data-testid="key-mc") clears memory to zero without affecting display
Memory indicator (data-testid="mem-indicator") shows data-active="true" when memory is non-zero, data-active="false" when zero
Memory starts at zero and respects number behaviour (stores exact value, displays rounded to 10 digits)
Memory keys do nothing in error state
AC leaves memory alone
M+ stores exact value (never rounded display text)
All keys behave correctly with negative numbers
sub_requirements: Implement M+ (adds display value to memory, finishes entry)
Implement MR (recalls memory as result)
Implement MC (clears memory)
Implement memory indicator with data-active attribute
Memory preserves exact values per agreed number behaviour
Memory unaffected by AC; memory keys inactive during error state

title: Final pass.
statement:
Final pass.

Keyboard entry:
- Digit keys and `.` type into the entry.
- `+`, `-`, `*`, `/` are the four operators.
- `Enter` or `=` is equals.
- `Escape` is clear.

Compact scientific mode:
- `data-testid="key-sci"` — a key that toggles a small scientific panel.
- While the panel is open it offers `data-testid="key-sqrt"` (√x), `data-testid="key-square"`
  (x²) and `data-testid="key-recip"` (1/x). Each acts on the current entry immediately:
  `9 √` shows `3`.

Then verify that nothing we built in earlier steps has broken, and fix anything that has.

title: Final pass: keyboard entry and compact scientific mode
statement: The calculator must support keyboard entry for digits, operators, equals and clear, plus a toggle for a compact scientific panel with √x, x², and 1/x operations.
acceptance: Digit keys and . type into the entry
Operators +, -, *, / are keyboard-accessible
Enter or = on keyboard triggers equals
Escape on keyboard triggers clear
SCI key toggles a small scientific panel open/closed
Panel offers √x, x² and 1/x buttons
Each scientific operation acts on current entry immediately (9 √ shows 3)
√ of negative number shows Error
1/0 shows Error
History records operations as √9, 9², 1/9
sub_requirements: Keyboard entry for basic operations
Compact scientific panel with three operations
Unary operation execution and error handling
Regression testing of earlier features
